claims.summary: McpHostEngine::load accepts a CapsuleContext but does not pass it into the connect_dynamic call.
claims.disposition: Exact at the report-bound SHA a1110a9b. mcp.rs:47 is `async fn load(&mut self, ctx: &CapsuleContext)`; the call at 162-164 is `self.mcp_client.connect_dynamic(&server_id, config)` with no ctx argument. Her cited 142-173 window covers it. ctx is used exactly once in load, at 143, `super::resolve_env(&self.manifest, ctx, &[], "mcp_host_engine")`.

Verified in current source, not in the report-bound file: context.rs:22 declares CapsuleContext and :44 `pub allowance_store: Option<Arc<astrid_approval::AllowanceStore>>`, default None at :73, set by `with_allowance_store` at :95. Optional, so a context may carry no store at all.

claims.summary: The mcp_client or McpHostEngine itself must already hold a reference to the context or the store.
claims.disposition: Contradicted by source; her underlying question stands. McpHostEngine's fields (mcp.rs:22-27) are manifest, server_def, capsule_dir, mcp_client only. SecureMcpClient's fields (secure.rs:43-52) are client, capabilities: Arc<CapabilityStore>, audit, session_id. Neither holds a CapsuleContext or an AllowanceStore. What authorizes connect_dynamic is SecureMcpClient's own CapabilityStore, a different store from the context's allowance_store.

claims.summary: She needs to confirm whether the struct definition includes the context or the mcp_client is initialized with it.
claims.disposition: Neither. The struct (mcp.rs:22-27) has no context field; `new` (29-42) takes an already-built SecureMcpClient. The construction site is loader.rs:53-65, inside `CapsuleLoader::create_capsule`, passing `self.mcp_client.clone()` — a loader-owned client, never derived from a CapsuleContext. The context reaches the engine only per-call as load(ctx).
